A: So, uh, let’s dive into the World Baseball Classic. I know a lot of folks are curious about Team Taiwan's journey this year. 

B: Oh, totally! I mean, it’s been a rollercoaster for them, right? They had some ups and downs, to say the least.

A: Right? They started off with a pretty rough patch, losing to Australia and then, oh man, that 13-0 blowout against Japan! Ouch!

B: I know! That had to be tough. But then they turned it around with that epic 5-4 win over Korea. That must’ve felt so good for them!

A: Absolutely! And the crowd at the Tokyo Dome was, like, super into it. You could feel the energy from Taiwan just radiating through the screen!

B: For sure! I mean, hitting a home run off Hyun Jin Ryu? That's something to brag about! 

A: Right? But, unfortunately, they couldn’t make it past the group stage. The tiebreaker rules were brutal. I mean, they were tied with Korea and Australia, and it all came down to runs allowed and outs made. 

B: Yeah, and it’s crazy how just a few runs could’ve changed everything for them. Like, one less run allowed in that opening game against Australia might’ve helped them advance!

A: Exactly! That’s the kind of stuff that really stings, you know? 

B: Totally. But hey, they managed to bounce back after that rough start, which says a lot about their resilience. 

A: Yeah! They really showed some heart. It’s a shame they’re out now, but hopefully, this experience will fuel them for the next WBC. 

B: Fingers crossed! It’ll be interesting to see how they build on this going forward. 

A: For sure. I mean, if they can learn from this tournament, who knows? They could be a serious contender next time around!

B: Exactly! And, you know, baseball is all about growth. They’ll take this experience and come back stronger. 

A: Alright, so, who do you think will be the team to beat now that Taiwan’s out?

B: Hmm, good question! I mean, Venezuela just won it all against the U.S. That’s huge! 

A: Oh, for sure! They’ve got some serious momentum going into the next round. 

B: Yeah, I can’t wait to see how this all plays out. Baseball drama at its finest! 

A: Definitely! Alright, let’s keep an eye on the rest of the tournament. Who knows what surprises are in store?

SOURCE TITLE: Taiwan eliminated from WBC following South Korea's 7-2 win over ...
SOURCE CONTENT: WBC / Taiwan eliminated from WBC following South Korea's 7-2 win over Australia
Taipei, March 9 (CNA) Team Taiwan's 2026 World Baseball Classic (WBC) journey ended Monday night when South Korea beat Australia 7-2 and won the tiebreaker with Australia and Taiwan to advance to the tournament's quarterfinals in Miami.
South Korea earned its spot by scoring a run in the top of the ninth to do just enough under the tiebreaker rules to advance.
The result saw Taiwan, South Korea, and Australia tied for second in WBC Pool C behind undefeated Japan with 2-2 records.
The tiebreaker was determined by dividing a team's total runs allowed by the total number of defensive outs in games among the tied teams, and with the three teams all allowing seven runs in their games, it came down to the smallest margin.
The Koreans got the nod because they recorded a total of 57 outs in their games against the tied teams (including a 10-inning 5-4 loss to Taiwan) while Taiwan and Australia recorded the regulation 54 outs.
Taiwan will rue its ugly start to the WBC, when it could muster only three hits in a 3-0 loss to Australia. Because Australia was the home team, Taiwan only recorded 24 outs, putting it at a disadvantage in determining who finished second.
A run scored or one fewer run allowed by Taiwan may have meant the difference in the final tiebreaker.
After an awful 13-0 loss in seven innings due to the mercy rule to Japan, Taiwan whipped the Czech Republic 14-0 in seven innings before outlasting South Korea 5-4 in 10 innings, giving it a sliver of hope of advancing.
In six WBCs played, Taiwan has only advanced to the quarterfinals once, in 2013.
Japan will complete Pool C play on Tuesday night against the Czech Republic, having already clinched the top spot in the group.

SOURCE TITLE: 2026 World Baseball Classic: Chinese Taipei Defeats Korea 5-4 in ...
SOURCE CONTENT: Chinese Taipei threw a wrench into Pool C of the World Baseball Classic on Sunday afternoon, edging Korea 5-4 in ten innings behind a strong start from Ruei-Yang Gu Lin and timely hitting.
Following two shutout losses to open the tournament, Chinese Taipei rebounded with two crucial wins and must await the results of Australia vs. Japan and Australia vs. Korea to determine whether they can advance to the quarterfinals via a second-place tiebreaker.
With Chinese Taipei’s win, Japan officially clinched a spot in the quarterfinals. Korea will face Australia tomorrow night. Australia controls its own destiny, but if it loses to Japan tonight, Korea’s hopes will remain alive. In that case, Korea would need a win to potentially advance through a tiebreaker.
Yu Chang opened the scoring with a solo home run off Hyun Jin Ryu in the second inning, igniting the packed Taiwanese crowd at the Tokyo Dome.
Korea chased Gu Lin from the game in the fifth and tied it when Shay Whitcomb bounced into a double play that brought home Hyun Min Ahn.
Tsung-Che Cheng put Chinese Taipei back in front in the sixth with a solo shot, but Do Yeong Kim answered with a towering two-run home run to left field off Wei-En Lin to give Korea its first lead of the day.
Gu Lin pitched admirably for Chinese Taipei, allowing just two hits and one run while working into the fifth inning on 59 pitches. Lin then added 2 ⅓ innings in relief, striking out four while allowing two runs.
Ryu went three innings for Korea, throwing 50 pitches and allowing one run on three hits with three strikeouts. Gwak Been followed with 3 ⅓ innings, giving up one run on two hits while striking out three.
